funding_tenor_analysis.text: `liquidity_scorecard_aggregation` answers "how healthy does our liquidity look overall?" by blending several individual metric scores into one weighted composite and mapping it to a RAG rating. You pass `scores` (one per component) and `weights`, which are normalised so they need not sum to 1. `funding_tenor_analysis` answers a narrower structural question: "how long-dated and stable is our funding base?" It takes `funding_amounts` and `tenors_days` for each tranche and returns the amount-weighted average tenor plus the share of funding maturing within 90 days. Put simply, the scorecard is a general roll-up of whatever metric scores you supply, while the tenor analysis computes one specific funding-profile metric from raw tranche data. The two can work together, since a tenor result could be one of the component scores you feed into the scorecard.

explain.text: `liquidity_scorecard_aggregation` (Liquidity Scorecard Aggregation) combines several individual liquidity metric scores into one weighted composite score. You pass `scores`, the component scores (each typically 0-100), and `weights`, one weight per component. The weights need not sum to 1 because pyvar normalises them. The composite is the sum of each score times its weight, divided by the sum of the weights. pyvar then maps that composite to a RAG (red/amber/green) rating, so you get a single summary view of liquidity health.

when.text:
Use Liquidity Scorecard Aggregation (`liquidity_scorecard_aggregation`) when you want one overall liquidity view built from several separate metrics:

- You already have individual component scores (typically 0-100) and need a single weighted composite in place of a pile of separate figures.
- Some metrics matter more than others in your view. `weights` let you express that, and they need not sum to 1 because pyvar normalises them.
- You want the composite mapped to a RAG rating, so the overall position is easy to communicate in a summary or dashboard.
- You want a transparent calculation: the composite is the weighted average of the `scores`, so it is easy to explain and to re-weight.
- For a different need, `funding_tenor_analysis` is listed as covering weighted-average funding tenor and short-term reliance.
